title: Push hasMention computation broken for application/jmap-chat-rich messages
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00.md, line 177

The push draft defines:

  `hasMention` (Boolean):
  : `true` if the account owner's ChatContact.id appears in the message's `mentions` array (a direct @user mention); `false` otherwise.

But the main draft (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 1257) states:

  When `bodyType` is `"application/jmap-chat-rich"`, `body` MUST contain a JSON-encoded string whose top-level parsed value is an object conforming to this section. The `mentions` array on the Message MUST be empty; mention information is carried inline within the spans.

Rich-body messages carry mention information in `spans[].userId` (where `spans[].type == "mention"`), not in `Message.mentions` (which is mandated empty). So a literal reading of the push draft's hasMention rule produces `false` for every rich-body message regardless of how many @user mentions appear inline. The notification routing logic and mentionUrgency escalation both depend on hasMention being correct.

Fix options:
1. Broaden the push-draft computation rule: "server MUST set hasMention to true if the account owner's ChatContact.id appears in Message.mentions OR (when bodyType is application/jmap-chat-rich) in any span of type \"mention\"."
2. Define hasMention in terms of an abstract "mentions resolved from the message" rather than the on-wire `Message.mentions` array, with a non-normative note pointing out the two storage locations.

Option 1 is more concrete and easier to validate; option 2 is more forward-compatible if a third mention-storage shape is added.

Relationship to fig9.4 (broadcast-scope mention payload updates): fig9.4 is about adding scope-typed broadcast mentions (@everyone, @here, @admins) to the payload. It is a different dimension (scope) from this finding (location: array vs inline spans). fig9.4 will likely revisit hasMention semantics, so this finding MAY be subsumed by fig9.4 work; if so, close as duplicate when fig9.4 lands. Pre-filing keeps the issue tracked in case fig9.4's scope stays narrow.
acceptance_criteria:
- Push draft hasMention rule covers BOTH the Message.mentions array path AND the application/jmap-chat-rich inline-spans path
- After the fix, a rich-body message containing a {type: mention, userId: <owner>} span produces hasMention=true on a push payload
- Add or extend an example payload (or the rich-body section) to demonstrate the rich-body mention case
- If fig9.4 lands first and naturally covers this case, close as duplicate of fig9.4 with a comment pointing at the resolution
